headline: US stocks fell hard overnight on an AI-chip selloff, but India looks set to open flat: oil fell almost 4% and foreign investors have been buying Indian shares for days. Today is a weekly expiry day, so expect choppy moves between about 25,000 and 25,500.

mood.label: Mixed
mood.why: The price trend is strongly up, but the put-call ratio dropped and option sellers have capped 25,500, so the dashboard's score is +16.5, just short of bullish, with only 1 of 4 steps agreeing. Overnight data as of 08:46 IST.

key_points.text: Overnight the US Nasdaq fell **2.5%** and chip stocks fell about 5%, and Asian markets are down 0.5–1.6% this morning. This is the main risk to the open.
Brent crude has fallen **3.9%** since India closed, to $91.7. India imports most of its oil, so cheaper oil helps prices, the rupee and company costs.
Foreign investors (FIIs) bought **₹4,865 crore** of Indian shares on Monday, their 5th straight day of buying, and about ₹84,000 crore so far in November.
My call: a **flat, sideways day** is more likely than a fall or a new high, with low confidence. India has been shrugging off global selling, but the rally is stretched and today is expiry day.

sections.title: What changed overnight
sections.summary: The night was bad for world stocks but good for oil, and the early signal for India is a flat open, so it neither undoes nor extends Monday's 0.6% gain.

points.text: GIFT Nifty (an overnight Nifty contract traded in Gujarat) was about **25,290–25,300** before 9 am, almost exactly where Nifty closed (25,291). Markets are pointing to a flat start.

US stocks: S&P 500 fell 1.9% and Nasdaq **2.5%**. Reports blame Nvidia's leadership turmoil after its CEO quit, new US limits on AI chip sales to China, and Fed Chair Warsh warning that an AI bust could cost jobs.
US futures are flat to slightly up this morning (Nasdaq futures **+0.4%**), so the selling has paused. They are still about 1.5% below where they were when India closed.
Asia is lower: Taiwan **−1.6%**, Japan −1.2%, Korea −1.1%, Hong Kong −0.9%. These are chip-heavy markets, which India is not.
Brent crude fell **3.9%** since India's close, on fears of too much oil supply. US bond rates, the dollar and the rupee (93.92 per dollar) barely moved overnight.

sections.title: Bounce or continuation?
sections.summary: After a strong up day, I expect a sideways session today rather than more gains or a sharp drop, with low confidence.

points.text: For more upside: FIIs keep buying in cash, oil is falling, and Monday India rose even though Korea fell 3.6%. India is being treated as a place to hide from the AI selloff. HDFC Bank's US shares even rose **1.8%** overnight.
Nifty futures rose while open bets fell **2.2%**. That means people who had bet on a fall were closing those bets, which pushes prices up.
For a pause or dip: Nifty is **6%** above its 20-day average after rising from about 22,700 to 25,291 in three weeks. That is a fast move and close to the last high of 25,424.
FIIs stopped adding new bets on a rise in index futures: their long share stayed at **34%** on Monday after jumping from 10.6% on 2 November.
What would prove me wrong: a close above **25,500** with FIIs adding new rise bets means the rally is continuing. A close below 25,000 means a real pullback has started.

sections.title: The big picture
sections.summary: The trend is clearly up, but option traders are less confident than a week ago.

points.text: Nifty is above its 20-, 50- and 200-day averages and is making higher highs and higher lows. The trend check gets the **maximum score (+2)**.
The put-call ratio (bets on a fall compared with bets on a rise) dropped from 1.47 to **1.03** in five sessions. The dashboard reads this as fewer people willing to back the market with sold puts.
Option sellers built a ceiling at **25,500** (the most call bets) and a floor at 25,000 (the most put bets). Neither level moved on Monday.
Fresh puts were sold at 25,200 and 25,300, which supports the market. But traders also bought puts at 24,800–25,000 as protection, so the option data is **slightly negative** overall.
India VIX (expected swings) is 15.7, higher than 71% of the past year but falling. Options are fairly expensive.

sections.title: What big investors are doing
sections.summary: Foreign money is coming in fast while Indian funds are taking profit.

points.text: FIIs bought a net **₹4,865 crore** in cash shares on Monday. That is about their average daily size lately, and their 5th buying day in a row.
Domestic funds (DIIs) sold **₹3,519 crore**. They have sold about ₹52,600 crore this month while FIIs bought about ₹84,200 crore, which is the reverse of October.

In index futures, FIIs still hold about **2 bets on a fall for every 1 on a rise** (34% long). There is room to close more of those fall bets, which could support prices, but they did not do so on Monday.
Reports link the buying to cheaper oil, better earnings and investors leaving crowded AI stocks. FIIs are still net sellers for 2026 overall, so the buying could reverse quickly.

sections.title: What the world is telling India
sections.summary: Cheaper oil helps India, but high US bond rates and the AI selloff are real risks.

points.text: Brent is down **16.5%** in a month. This is the single biggest help for India right now and the main reason the dashboard's world check reads favourable.
The US 10-year bond rate is 5.13%, up **0.27 points** this week. When US bonds pay this much, foreign money has less reason to buy Indian shares.
Short-term US bond prices suggest the market now expects the Fed's **next move to be a rate hike**, not a cut. That would usually pull money away from countries like India.
The US fear gauge (VIX) jumped **19%** to 22.9. When US investors get scared, they often sell abroad too.
The rupee is about 1.1% stronger than a month ago at **93.92** per dollar, which makes Indian shares worth more to foreign investors.

sections.title: Company results
sections.summary: Recent Nifty 50 results are a mixed bag, and most big reporting is now done.

points.text: Eicher Motors: revenue up 20%, profit up **15%** from a year ago. That is solid, though it does not meet the dashboard's 'strong' bar of 20%.
Grasim: revenue up 26% but profit down **31%**, so costs grew much faster than sales.

Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles made a loss of about **₹5,451 crore**. The year-ago profit was inflated by a one-time gain from splitting the company, so the 107% fall exaggerates the problem. I couldn't confirm how the stock reacted.
No Nifty 50 company reports in the next week. The big result to watch is **Nvidia**, after the US close tonight (early Wednesday in India).

sections.title: What could change the picture
sections.summary: The next few days are about US tech and US rates more than India's own news.

points.text: Nvidia's results come early Wednesday India time. A good report could calm the AI selloff. A bad one could drag world markets lower again, though India has been holding up.
US retail sales at **7 pm IST** today and Fed meeting minutes at 12:30 am Thursday IST. Strong numbers would add to fears of a US rate hike.
The monthly F&O expiry is on **23 November**, and markets are shut on 24 November for Guru Nanak Jayanti.
India GDP on 30 November, RBI policy on **4 December**, Fed decision early 10 December IST.
If FIIs turn sellers again, it would undo the main reason for the rally, especially with domestic funds already selling.

levels.note: A close above 25,500 would mean call sellers have given up and the rally is extending. A close below 25,000 would break the main support and point to a deeper pullback.

watch.text: The first 15 minutes: does Nifty hold near 25,290, or do Asia's losses pull it down?
Weekly expiry close: option bets at 25,200–25,500 can cause sharp moves late in the day.
Provisional FII and DII figures: a 6th day of FII buying would support the rally.
US retail sales: strong numbers would push US bond rates higher, which is bad for foreign flows into India.
Nvidia results after the US close (early Wednesday India time).

bottom_line: The trend is up and foreign money is flowing in, helped by much cheaper oil. But the dashboard's checks don't agree (score +16.5, just short of bullish, with low conviction): option traders have capped 25,500 and the put-call ratio has dropped. With US tech falling and the GIFT Nifty flat, my read is a sideways expiry day between 25,000 and 25,500. The main risk is the AI selloff spreading, or a bad Nvidia report, turning FIIs back into sellers.
